Handoff: local BLUP calibration implementation

Source: handoff.md

Use this note to guide implementation of the RSYC local BLUP-based calibration in another project. The most important point is that the implementation lives primarily in the BLUP helper script, not in the full curve-assignment pipeline.

Primary files

  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9998_blupCalibration.R
    • This is the main reference implementation.
    • Start here for the functions to port or adapt:
      • RSYC_blup_load_model_components() near line 84
      • RSYC_blup_prepare_components() near line 181
      • RSYC_blup_assign_curve() near line 364
      • RSYC_blup_calibrate() near line 704
    • The delivered calibrated value is assigned near line 1329: AGB_RSYC_BLUP = blup_curve_value_assigned * ratio_BLUP.
  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9999_curveAssign.R
    • Use this as calling-context only, not as the main implementation to port.
    • It shows how the BLUP helper is wired into the broader RSYC curve assignment.
    • Relevant settings are near lines 68-99: min_valid_AGB, use_blup_calibration, blup_model_dir, blup_response_col, caps, and screening thresholds.
    • The actual call to RSYC_blup_calibrate() is near lines 836-864.
    • The older ratio-based local calibration is near lines 601-835; this is useful for comparison but is not the preferred single-measurement method.

Useful examples and diagnostics

  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/1100_test_blup_calibration_single_tile.R
    • Prototype/test implementation for running BLUP calibration on one tile.
    • Useful if the new project needs a smaller, more explicit example than the full production helper.
  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/1101_diagnose_blup_shrinkage_drivers.R
    • Diagnostic script that recomputes the BLUP ingredients: sum_gd, sum_g2, n_obs, A_i, residual_var / pixel_var, and the shrinkage factor.
    • Useful for validating that a ported implementation produces the same shrinkage behavior.
  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/1102_diagnose_rsyc_models.R
    • Diagnostic script for checking model variance components and model health.
  • K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/HANDOFF_blup_tamarack_fix.md
    • Context for why caps and model screening were added.
    • Important if reproducing the robust production behavior rather than a bare BLUP formula.

Behavior to reproduce

The BLUP calibration estimates a local pixel-level random effect for each IDpix, AgeClass, blup_model_species group. It uses observed AGB at known age to estimate a level adjustment, then applies that adjustment as a ratio to the assigned RSYC curve.

For one observation, the estimate is still valid because min_valid_AGB defaults to 1, but the result should be treated as a shrinkage-based local level anchor, not as a learned local growth trajectory.

Core coefficient logic in RSYC_blup_calibrate():

blup_sum_gd = sum(blup_g_obs * (blup_response - blup_base_obs), na.rm = TRUE)
blup_sum_g2 = sum(blup_g_obs^2, na.rm = TRUE)

blup_shrinkage_factor =
  blup_sum_g2 / (blup_sum_g2 + blup_residual_var / blup_pixel_var)

blup_b_pixel =
  blup_sum_gd / (blup_sum_g2 + blup_residual_var / blup_pixel_var)

ratio_BLUP = (blup_A_i + blup_b_pixel) / blup_A_i
AGB_RSYC_BLUP = blup_curve_value_assigned * ratio_BLUP

With a single plot measurement, this becomes a one-point adjustment:

blup_b_pixel =
  g(age) * (AGB_observed - base_AGB_at_age) /
  (g(age)^2 + residual_var / pixel_var)

The residual_var / pixel_var term is what shrinks weak local evidence toward no adjustment.

Required input fields

The new project does not need to reproduce the entire tile pipeline, but it must create an input table with the fields needed by RSYC_blup_calibrate() or an adapted equivalent:

  • IDpix: local pixel or stand identifier.
  • AgeClass: segment identifier used with IDpix; in the original workflow this separates stand trajectory segments.
  • age: plot or pixel age at the observation year.
  • AGB: observed or externally supplied aboveground biomass response.
  • isTreed: 1L for observations eligible for calibration.
  • is_projected: optional; projected observations are excluded by default.
  • species: species code/name used to select a species-specific model when available.
  • type: broad species group, with "C" for conifer and "D" for broadleaf.
  • AGB_RSYC_species, AGB_RSYC_coniferous, AGB_RSYC_broadleaf, AGB_RSYC_generic: assigned RSYC curve values for the observation/prediction rows.
  • Case: original workflow state; rows with Case == 0L or missing age are not assigned a BLUP model species.

The model components must provide fixed effects, tile random effect, pixel random-effect variance, and residual variance. In the original implementation these are loaded from nlme model .rds files via RSYC_blup_load_model_components().

Recommended implementation path

  1. Port/adapt RSYC_blup_g(), RSYC_blup_assign_curve(), RSYC_blup_prepare_components(), and RSYC_blup_calibrate() from K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9998_blupCalibration.R.

  2. If the new project cannot use the same nlme model .rds objects, replace only the component-loading layer. Preserve the downstream component columns: blup_beta1, blup_beta2, blup_beta3, blup_beta4, blup_tile_b1, blup_pixel_var, blup_residual_var, and blup_component_ok.

  3. Keep the production safeguards unless there is a deliberate reason not to: random-effect cap, blup_ratio_max, AGB hard cap, and model health checks.

  4. Validate the port using the diagnostic formulas in K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/1101_diagnose_blup_shrinkage_drivers.R. The same inputs should produce the same blup_sum_gd, blup_sum_g2, blup_shrinkage_factor, blup_b_pixel, and ratio_BLUP.

  5. For users with only one plot measurement, document the output as a “single-observation BLUP-anchored RSYC curve” or similar. Avoid saying that the local growth trajectory has been learned from one point.

Short answer on which file to show first

Do not point the other assistant only at K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9999_curveAssign.R. Point it first at K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9998_blupCalibration.R, then use K:/_PROJECTS/RSYC_curvePerPixel/R/9999_curveAssign.R to show how the helper is called inside the full RSYC pipeline.
